rows.note: In the ayah al-ʿaṣr means time or the late afternoon, while Biblical Hebrew עצר means to restrain or detain and also gives the noun for a solemn assembly.

rows.explanation: עצרני means “has kept me from” bearing children, showing the Hebrew sense of restraint.
עצר עצר describes the LORD closing the wombs of Abimelech’s household, showing the Hebrew sense of holding back.
עצרת names a solemn assembly on the eighth day, a Hebrew sense distinct from the ayah’s “time.”
